text: In the first year the prisoner suffered terribly. <break time="0.8s" /> From loneliness and boredom. <break time="0.8s" /> Day and night. <break time="0.8s" /> The piano could be heard. <break time="0.8s" /> From his room. <break time="0.8s" /> And he read only light, easy novels. <break time="0.8s" /> In the second year. <break time="0.8s" /> The music stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> And he asked only for the great classics. <break time="0.8s" /> In the sixth year. <break time="0.8s" /> He began studying. <break time="0.8s" /> Languages, philosophy, and history. <break time="0.8s" /> With great passion. <break time="0.8s" /> The banker hardly had time. <break time="0.8s" /> To order the books. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked for. <break time="0.8s" /> In four years. <break time="0.8s" /> About six hundred books. <break time="0.8s" /> Were sent to him. <break time="0.8s" /> Later he wrote. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had learned six languages. <break time="0.8s" /> And that his soul. <break time="0.8s" /> Was filled with joy. <break time="0.8s" /> After that he read the Bible. <break time="0.8s" /> And books about religion. <break time="0.8s" /> For a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> In the last two years. <break time="0.8s" /> He read everything. <break time="0.8s" /> Without any order. <break time="0.8s" /> Science one day. <break time="0.8s" /> And poetry the next. <break time="0.8s" /> He read like a drowning man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who grabs at one piece of wood after another.
